description: Capabilities for the floating-iPhone simulator windows (label simulator-*): drag the frame to move, focus, close, DESTROY, minimize, resize (rotate), render the live session webview, and persist the handed-off API base URL plus session recordings. This grant is NOT minimal any more. The earlier description advertised windowing, webview and events only, and that had quietly stopped being true: SimulatorWindow calls persistBaseUrl (plugin-store) on mount, and when that call is denied authedFetch falls back to localhost:3000 and every control call fails. Nothing caught it because these windows had been deleted; they exist again on Windows and Linux, where there is no separate Simulator app. The grant now mirrors EXACTLY what simulator-app.json already gives the separate app's sim-* windows -- the same view, so the same needs -- and nothing beyond them. The account API key is NOT reachable from here and widening this file cannot change that: secret_save/secret_load/secret_delete are gated in Rust by secret_command_caller_allowed -> is_main_gui_command_caller, which requires the window label to be exactly "main". core:window:allow-destroy is not optional next to allow-close: Tauri calls api.prevent_close() the moment a window has a JS onCloseRequested listener and hands the real close to JavaScript, whose only mechanism is destroy(). Without it every close path dead-ends in a denied command that rejects inside Tauri's fire-and-forget listen callback -- an unhandled rejection that paints the full-screen fatal overlay over the in-content toolbar. Since the window is decorations:false, that toolbar holds the only close and minimize buttons, so the window becomes unclosable and undraggable; the main window cannot close it either, because ACL is evaluated against the CALLING window and default.json grants neither. Escape was a Task Manager kill.
